title: Europa's Hidden Ocean and the Clipper Mission
description: Europa hides a salty ocean beneath thick ice, potentially holding twice Earth's water. The Europa Clipper will explore it with dozens of close flybys.

shots.narration: This frozen moon may hold about twice the water of all Earth's oceans.
Europa Clipper lifted off on fourteen October 2024, the largest NASA planetary spacecraft ever built.
Its solar arrays span about thirty metres, capturing sunlight for the long journey to Jupiter.
Europa's surface is cracked water ice, streaked with reddish lines across a moon slightly smaller than ours.
Beneath fifteen to twenty‑five kilometres of ice, a salty ocean stays liquid, kept warm by Jupiter's tidal flexing.
Juno flew three hundred fifty kilometres above Europa in September 2022, photographing its icy surface.
When it arrives in 2030, the Clipper will perform forty‑nine close flybys, some as low as twenty‑five kilometres.
The launch vehicle lifted the spacecraft beyond Earth's gravity, beginning its journey toward the icy world.
Europa may hold about twice the water of all Earth's oceans, a remarkable reservoir beneath its ice.
